audit.whatIsWrong: Five rows contradicted the page's own why-strings: the chart gave Yorick levels 3, 4-5, first item and 2+ items and called level 2 Skill, while whys say 'Level 2 stays hers', 'Level 3 is skill', 'Levels 4-5 are even', 'First item favours Lillia' and 'Late she out-DoTs your ghouls... keeping the fight hers'.
audit.why: The packet chart reads Lillia, Lillia, Skill, Skill, Lillia, Lillia, Lillia and matches those whys row for row. Two independent sources against the sides layer, and the matchup sits at 50.16% only because Yorick converts the map, not the lane.
audit.corrected: win[1] to Lillia, win[2] and win[3] to Skill, win[5] and win[6] to Lillia, each with its phases[N].side pair; ratings 3/10, 5/10, 5/10, 3/10, 3/10. diff EVEN to HARD to match tone and difficulty 7.5/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[1..3], [5] and [6] were generic boilerplate that claimed Yorick spikes on rows that belong to Lillia.
audit.why: Lillia's spikes are Blooming Blows stacking move speed from level 1 (6s at rank 1), Lilting Lullaby at 6 (150s at rank 1), and her first AP item, which lets her poke and simply outrun Mourning Mist's slow. Yorick's only real window is a landed mark on 12s that speeds the ghouls onto her, and Maiden pressure on towers.
audit.corrected: Rewrote phases[1].why, phases[2].why, phases[3].why, phases[5].why and phases[6].why to those spikes with cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Flagged defect — no cooldowns anywhere, and the page never mentions the two interactions that decide the lane: Lilting Lullaby only affects enemies already carrying Dream Dust, and Swirlseed rolls until it hits a wall.
audit.why: Riot's text for the ultimate: 'Lillia causes all enemies with Dream Dust on them to become Drowsy.' Dream Dust comes from her passive on spell hits, so if none of her spells have touched you, her 150s ultimate does nothing to you — that is the whole counterplay and it was missing. Swirlseed 'will continue rolling until it hits a wall or target', and Dark Procession is a wall, so your own 20s cage eats it. Blooming Blows deals extra TRUE damage on the edge, so the rim is the dangerous part of the ring and stacking resistances misreads the trade.
audit.corrected: Dream Dust gating, Swirlseed vs the wall, the true-damage rim and all three cooldowns into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[1].d and report[5].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: Lillia is referred to as 'he' or 'him' in nine places, including the TL;DR and the win condition.
audit.why: Lillia is female; the mixed pronouns read as copy from another matchup and undercut trust in the rest of the page.
audit.corrected: Pronouns fixed in tldr, winCon, the two matching report entries, breakdown.wave, breakdown.feeding, breakdown.late, the don'ts and report[11].
